title: Tech Note: SQL to ORDA
author: Kristopher Merolla, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note captures ORDA at its very first public release in v17 (2018), before the object/dataclass/entity model matured with computed attributes, remote datastores, dataclass functions, and the eventual REST-first architecture; the fundamentals shown (ds, dataclass, entity selections, new()/save()/lock()) remain accurate and are still the core ORDA vocabulary today. The SQL-vs-ORDA framing itself is dated in spirit since 4D now actively steers new development toward ORDA/collections rather than presenting them as parallel equally-weighted options.
related_updates: ORDA gained many additional member functions, computed/alias/related attributes, and dataclass class functions in v18-v20
4D now recommends ORDA (with classes and formulas) as the primary data-access layer; classic SQL/QUERY remain supported mainly for legacy code
Locking and CRUD conventions described are still valid today
